catalog.definition: Wholesale electricity price — its level (shift) and volatility (spread).
catalog.label: Electricity price

catalog.definition: Regional grid load. High demand → tighter reserves, higher prices, more DR.
catalog.label: Grid demand

catalog.definition: How aggressively the battery charges from surplus + discharges at peak.
catalog.label: BESS aggressiveness

catalog.definition: Frequency of utility demand-response calls (load-shed events).
catalog.label: DR call likelihood

catalog.definition: Frequency of grid brownouts / voltage sags on the feeder.
catalog.label: Brownout rate

catalog.definition: Frequency of grid Hz excursions outside the nominal band.
catalog.label: Frequency excursion

catalog.definition: Grid gCO2/kWh level (generation-mix dirtiness).
catalog.label: Carbon intensity

catalog.definition: Outside air temperature. Drives charging derate, BESS thermal, solar cell temp, DR likelihood.
catalog.label: Ambient temperature

catalog.definition: Daily precipitation total (real NOAA GHCND, Nashville). Drives wet-day couplings: more & worse ETA delays.
catalog.label: Precipitation (daily)

catalog.definition: How overcast it is. Directly suppresses solar generation.
catalog.label: Cloud cover

catalog.definition: Wind speed. Cools panels + battery slightly.
catalog.label: Wind speed

catalog.definition: Relative humidity. Affects fog/visibility + perception-fault likelihood.
catalog.label: Humidity

catalog.definition: Likelihood + intensity of rain/snow. Cuts solar, raises incident + perception-fault rates.
catalog.label: Precipitation

catalog.definition: Dust/haze on panels reducing output between rain washes.
catalog.label: Solar soiling

catalog.definition: How often vehicles arrive at and deploy from the depot.
catalog.label: Arrival / dispatch rate

catalog.definition: Mid-trip congestion / accident that pushes a deployed vehicle's return ETA out.
catalog.label: Arrival ETA delay

catalog.definition: Extra battery drain while a car is out, in SoC points per hour deployed: -30 drains 30 more points each hour, so cars come back lower. Lower = more charging demand. Only negative values act: driving refills nothing.
catalog.label: SoC on arrival

catalog.definition: Charge level vehicles aim for before redeploying.
catalog.label: Target SoC

catalog.definition: Length of deployment trips (drives how long vehicles are away).
catalog.label: Trip duration

catalog.definition: Proportion of the active fleet that is Tesla (vs Waymo/Zoox). Shifts charging-curve + connector mix.
catalog.label: Tesla share

catalog.definition: Multiplier on active-driving fraction. Lower = more idling / staging time, less discharge + exposure.
catalog.label: Drive-activity level

catalog.definition: Charge-session duration factor (slower/faster than calibrated).
catalog.label: Charge duration

catalog.definition: Exterior-wash duration factor.
catalog.label: Wash duration

catalog.definition: Interior-detail duration factor.
catalog.label: Detail duration

catalog.definition: Light-maintenance duration factor.
catalog.label: Maintenance duration

catalog.definition: Overall staffing as a fraction of full. 1.0 = fully staffed (no bottleneck); lower = understaffed → vehicles wait in staging until lanes free.
catalog.label: Staffing level

catalog.definition: Staff for charging assist (2 per 10 vehicles at full). Lower throttles concurrent charge starts.
catalog.label: Charging-assist staff

catalog.definition: Staff for wash/detail bays (2 per bay at full). Lower → fewer concurrent washes.
catalog.label: Cleaning staff

catalog.definition: Staff for service+maintenance bays (2 per bay at full). Lower → fewer concurrent service jobs.
catalog.label: Service/maint staff

catalog.definition: Staff to release staged vehicles for redeployment (2 per vehicle, final segment). Lower → vehicles linger in staging.
catalog.label: Deploy-prep staff

catalog.definition: How long a vehicle waits in queue before OTTO-Q reroutes it.
catalog.label: Queue patience

catalog.definition: Which scheduling strategy OTTO-Q uses to assign stalls.
catalog.label: OTTO-Q scheduling policy

catalog.definition: How often chargers fault mid-session (ChargerHelp-calibrated baseline).
catalog.label: Charger fault rate

catalog.definition: Vehicle diagnostic-trouble-code spawn rate (DMV-calibrated).
catalog.label: DTC / fault-code rate

catalog.definition: On-road incident rate (collisions/breakdowns, DMV-calibrated).
catalog.label: Incident rate

catalog.definition: Shifts the mix toward more severe incidents (more tows/majors).
catalog.label: Incident severity

catalog.definition: Rate of partial/dropped telemetry packets (degraded comms).
catalog.label: Telemetry dropout

catalog.definition: How widely battery state-of-health varies across the fleet.
catalog.label: Battery-health spread

catalog.definition: Rate of disabling breakdowns requiring a tow.
catalog.label: Breakdown / tow rate

catalog.definition: Per-vehicle usable battery health; scales usable capacity + charge acceptance
catalog.label: Battery health (SoH)

catalog.definition: Per-vehicle drive-energy multiplier (driving style, drivetrain wear, HVAC bias)
catalog.label: Energy consumption scalar

catalog.definition: Per-vehicle multiplier on delivered charge power (pack chemistry age, BMS caps)
catalog.label: Charge-curve scalar

catalog.definition: Per-vehicle soil accrual multiplier (routes, districts, ride profile)
catalog.label: Soiling rate

catalog.definition: Per-vehicle preventive-maintenance due distance
catalog.label: PM interval

catalog.definition: Per-vehicle drive-hours between sensor calibrations
catalog.label: Sensor calibration interval

catalog.definition: Per-vehicle service-time multiplier (access quirks, trim, sensor count)
catalog.label: Service duration scalar

catalog.definition: Deploy cycles between exterior washes for this vehicle
catalog.label: Wash cadence

datasets.description: Billions of real for-hire-vehicle trips. Calibrates arrival rate by hour-of-day, day-of-week, seasonality.
datasets.ingestion_notes: Ingested yellow_tripdata_2024-06: 3539142 in-range trips. Hourly + DoW arrival profiles + trip-duration distribution.

datasets.description: 130,000+ real EV charging sessions with arrival/departure times, energy requested + delivered, charge durations.
datasets.ingestion_notes: Ingested 4000 real EV charging sessions from ACN-Data (Caltech + JPL). Charge-duration, energy-delivered, dwell-time distributions + hourly/DoW arrival profiles + dwell~energy correlation.
datasets.what_it_calibrates: charge_duration_minutes, energy_delivered_kwh, dwell_time_minutes, soc-vs-time charging curves

datasets.description: Real commercial fleet operational behavior — duty cycles, daily energy, dwell patterns.
datasets.ingestion_notes: Encoded from NREL Fleet DNA published aggregate statistics. Daily energy lognormal (mean 50 kWh), miles normal (mean 120), idle-fraction beta(2, 4.5).
datasets.source_name: NREL Fleet DNA + EV Charging Datasets

datasets.description: Real hourly grid demand, generation mix, and interchange by balancing authority (TVA region for Nashville).
datasets.ingestion_notes: Live refit via ottoq-twin-ingest: 8784 values for grid_demand_mw

datasets.description: Real annual autonomous-vehicle disengagement and collision data from CA-permitted AV operators.
datasets.ingestion_notes: Encoded from published CA DMV AV disengagement + collision report aggregates (2022-2024). Miles-per-disengagement modeled as lognormal (median 5000 mi, sigma=1.4); cause mix and severity mix from industry-aggregate published findings.
datasets.source_name: California DMV Autonomous Vehicle Disengagement + Collision Reports

datasets.description: Composite of published EV charger reliability + uptime studies — real fault rates, failure-mode mix.
datasets.ingestion_notes: Encoded from composite published EV charger reliability studies (UC Berkeley 2022 Bay Area, JD Power EVX, ChargerHelp). Uptime beta(15,5) ~75% mean; MTBF lognormal 30d median; session success beta(16,4) ~80% mean; fault mode mix from ChargerHelp.
datasets.source_org: UC Berkeley / JD Power / academic literature

datasets.description: Monthly wet-day Markov chain (p01 = P(wet|dry yesterday), p11 = P(wet|wet yesterday)) and empirical wet-day amount distributions computed directly from 10,956 QC-filtered daily precipitation observations, 1991-2020. Wet day = >=0.2mm. Includes the May 2010 flood (184.2mm) in the May tail.
datasets.source_name: GHCN-Daily Nashville BNA (USW00013897) — computed precipitation structure
datasets.what_it_calibrates: precip_mm daily budget card (Markov occurrence + monthly amount grids precip_wet_mm month:01..12), hourly disaggregation, ETA/incident cascade, wash demand, solar soiling

datasets.description: Official NOAA 30-year climate normals for Nashville International Airport: monthly mean daily max/min/avg temperature, NOAA-published within-month stddev of daily average temp (DLY-TAVG-STDDEV), record extremes (1873-present thread), and GHCN-Daily-computed lag-1 autocorrelation of daily mean anomalies (phi=0.72, n=10,958).
datasets.what_it_calibrates: ambient_temp_c monthly-conditioned distributions (segments month:01..month:12), per-month diurnal amplitude, AR(1) day-to-day persistence

datasets.description: Live + recent real weather observations for the depot location (Nashville).
datasets.ingestion_notes: Live refit via ottoq-twin-ingest: 362 values for precip_mm

provenance.ar1_method: lag-1 Pearson r of deseasonalized daily means, GHCN-Daily 1991-2020, n=10958; monthly phis 0.69-0.80 (summer stickier); WGEN literature range 0.6-0.8
provenance.ghcn_qc_warning: raw GHCN parsing REQUIRES QFLAG filtering (unfiltered parse produced a bogus -40C value)
provenance.grid_method: quantile grids generated from Normal(mean, sigma) per month, clamped to record extremes; parametric-through-grid, declared
provenance.records_period: 1873-present (NWS thread); 21/24 extremes match BNA-only GHCN recompute
provenance.sigma_method: NOAA published DLY-TAVG-STDDEV (within-month mean), cross-validated against GHCN-Daily anomalies within 0.2C every month

declared_assumptions.name: depot_grade_fault_discount
declared_assumptions.why: fitted public-network session failure is 0.20; a maintained private depot with daily utilization and on-site staff is assumed 4x more reliable -> base 0.05, matching prior world behavior but now sourced and tunable

declared_assumptions.name: depot_staffed_factor
declared_assumptions.why: fitted repair_days reflect public-network truck-roll logistics (mean 7.3 DAYS); a staffed depot with on-site technician and parts is assumed ~50x faster -> mean ~3.5h, median ~2.3h, long tail to 48h preserved via the fitted grid shape

provenance.corpus: MISO DA ex-post LMP CSVs 2024-01-01..2026-06-30 (912 files, 21,888 hourly prices/hub) + 183-day RT sample
provenance.cross_check: INDIANA.HUB 2025 $43.73 (upper bracket, +30% northern congestion); PJM Western Hub 2025 DA ~$42; MISO all-in 2024 $31 (Potomac Economics SOM)

declared_assumptions.name: tva_proxy
declared_assumptions.why: TVA is not in an RTO and publishes no spot prices; ARKANSAS.HUB borders TVA at the west-Tennessee seam with the same gas-heavy southern stack — the most defensible public proxy

declared_assumptions.name: cheap_threshold_22
declared_assumptions.why: p5=14.86 and mean=33; 22 approximates p25 (charge-cheap trigger); expensive=51.08 is the computed p95 (discharge trigger)

declared_assumptions.name: symmetric_day_regime
declared_assumptions.why: day-to-day drift modeled as symmetric multiplier around the seasonal mean, clamped 0.6-1.8; matches observed day-mean dispersion to first order

declared_assumptions.name: temp_coupling_scaled_down
declared_assumptions.why: legacy +$8/MWh per degC above 30 was unsourced and hot; scaled to +1.5 heat / +3.0 cold as a scarcity proxy consistent with winter-peaking evidence

live_refresh.secondary: EIA API v2 electricity/wholesale-prices (daily ICE trade data, free key required)

provenance.trend_warning: ARK mean +37 pct 2024->2025, +8 pct into 2026H1 (gas +56 pct); baseline set to 2025, agent should revisit against 2026 actuals

declared_assumptions.name: hourly_disaggregation
declared_assumptions.why: hourly precipitation observations are not in the corpus; wet-window length by daily budget and the summer-afternoon convective bias are climatological assumptions, declared and tunable

declared_assumptions.name: intensity_jitter
declared_assumptions.why: within-window hourly intensity varies +/-60 pct around budget/hours; unbiased to first order

provenance.method: first-order two-state Markov chain per month (WGEN family, Richardson & Wright USDA); amounts = empirical monthly quantile grids over wet days (n=233-349/mo)
provenance.notable: May 2010 flood (184.2mm) present in the May tail; September is the driest month (p_wet 0.259), February the wettest (0.381)

provenance.basis: OTTOQ_SERVICE_OPS_RESEARCH cadence model (camera-triggered probabilistic cleaning validated by Waymo Bayview depot reporting); the numbers are explicitly tunable assumptions pending a real fleet-servicing corpus
provenance.coupling_evidence: rain->dirtier vehicles: precip_stress from the unified GHCN Markov daily card multiplies cleaning probabilities by (1 + stress * 0.6), capped at 0.90
provenance.future: mileage-based sensor_calibration/mechanical_pm using NREL daily_miles (fitted, unused) once vehicle odometer state exists

provenance.cross_check: KUB Knoxville GSA-3 (same TVA family): summer $20.22/$20.96, winter $19.46/$20.20 — NES squarely in-family
provenance.headline_implication: prior $10/kW assumption understates Nashville ~2x; a 1,000 kW shave prices at ~$21.8k/mo summer / ~$20.7k/mo winter at real NES marginal rates — re-certify the $ headline via CRN A/B before quoting

provenance.notes: GSA Part 3: contract demand >1,000 kW and <=5,000 kW. Demand basis = non-coincident peak (highest 30-consecutive-minute kW in the billing month) — the depot shaving its OWN monthly max directly cuts the bill. Billing floor 30% of max(contract demand, prior-12-mo high). Energy base excludes the monthly TVA fuel-cost adjustment (~2.8-4c/kWh). URDB values are FCA-inclusive and diverge slightly from the PDF — the NES PDF is authoritative. A further ~4.5% TVA increase for Oct 2025 is claimed by a secondary source, unconfirmed by primary (MEDIUM confidence).
Winter billing months Dec-Mar; same structure as summer row.
Transition billing months Apr, May, Oct, Nov; TVA prices these at winter rates.
